repositories.scope: Local coding agent and its application integration surface

questions.question: What is Codex CLI and how is it started?
facts: A coding agent that runs locally.
After installation, run codex.

questions.question: What handshake does codex app-server require?
facts: Default transport is newline-delimited JSON over stdio.
Send initialize then initialized before other requests.

questions.question: How does a client drive a conversation?
facts: Start or resume a thread, then call turn/start.
Progress arrives as notifications; completion includes final state and token usage.

questions.question: Is WebSocket transport production-supported?
facts: WebSocket is experimental and unsupported.
The documentation says not to rely on it for production workloads.

questions.question: Where are safety and vulnerability-reporting boundaries documented?
facts: Linked security documentation covers sandbox, approvals and network controls.
Validated vulnerabilities should be reported through Bugcrowd.

repositories.scope: Bitcoin Core full node with optional wallet and GUI

questions.question: What does Bitcoin Core provide?
facts: Connects to the Bitcoin P2P network and fully validates blocks and transactions.
Wallet and GUI support are optional to build.

questions.question: How does an application access the RPC API?
facts: bitcoind enables JSON-RPC by default; bitcoin-qt disables it by default.
The API exposes / and /wallet/<walletname>/ endpoints.

questions.question: How are runtime configuration changes applied?
facts: Command-line options override bitcoin.conf.
Configuration-file changes require restart.

questions.question: What deployment costs are stated?
facts: Default full-history storage needs several hundred gigabytes or more.
Initial synchronization may take hours to several days or more.

questions.question: How are release binaries verified?
facts: Checksums are evaluated against signatures from selected trusted keys.
The verifier returns 0 on success and 1 on signature or hash failure.

repositories.scope: Shell-output compression proxy for reducing agent context consumption

questions.question: What problem does RTK solve?
facts: Compresses shell-command output before an agent reads it, reducing token consumption.
It is a single Rust binary; documentation claims 100+ commands and overhead below 10 ms.

questions.question: How is RTK connected to Codex?
facts: Run rtk init -g --codex.
Integration installs under CODEX_HOME, falling back to ~/.codex/.

questions.question: How are savings measured and exported?
facts: rtk gain --all --format json exports machine-readable statistics.
History is local at ~/.local/share/rtk/history.db with 90-day retention.

questions.question: What do token statistics not guarantee?
facts: Estimates use bytes / 4, not a real tokenizer.
Absolute estimates do not match provider billing.

questions.question: How can missed adoption be identified?
facts: rtk discover finds command history without RTK filtering.
rtk session reports RTK-versus-raw command coverage.

repositories.scope: HTTP client library for browsers and Node.js

questions.question: What is Axios and how is it installed?
facts: Promise-based HTTP client for browser and Node.js.
Install with npm install axios.

questions.question: What public API supports custom adapters and client instances?
facts: AxiosAdapter accepts internal request config and returns AxiosPromise.
AxiosInstance supports request calls and create(config).

questions.question: How should request timeouts be handled?
facts: timeout is in milliseconds and aborts an overdue request.
Without a timeout a stalled request can hang indefinitely.

questions.question: What security assumptions must callers handle?
facts: Default maxContentLength and maxBodyLength are unlimited.
baseURL constructs URLs; it is not a security boundary for untrusted URLs.

questions.question: For an attested Axios release, what does provenance verification establish?
facts: npm provenance binds the tarball to the GitHub Actions workflow and commit SHA.
npm audit signatures verifies provenance, not absence of bugs.

questions.question: What is n8n?
facts: A platform for AI agents and workflow automation.
Combines a visual canvas and custom code, with self-hosted or cloud deployment.

questions.question: What are the documented quick-start entry points?
facts: npx n8n provides a Node.js-based start path.
Docker exposes the editor at http://localhost:5678.

questions.question: Which process modes are exposed by the repository package?
facts: The webhook script invokes packages/cli/bin/n8n webhook.
The worker script invokes packages/cli/bin/n8n worker.

questions.question: What licensing restrictions affect source use?
facts: Non-Enterprise source is governed by the Sustainable Use License.
Files or directories containing .ee require a valid n8n Enterprise License.

questions.question: How does the documented Sentry transaction hook sample production webhooks?
facts: Successful production webhook transactions may be sampled down to webhook.sampleRate.
Errored webhook transactions are exempt from this webhook sampling rule; this is not a guarantee of end-to-end telemetry retention.
